name: How We Tamed the Wild
description: From the first wolf at the campfire to the banana in the supermarket: the animals and crops that people bred and that changed human life.

checkpoints.name: First partners
checkpoints.note: Wolves become dogs at the camps of hunters, and then people in the Near East begin to farm wheat and barley and keep goats, sheep, pigs and cattle.

checkpoints.name: Fields and herds
checkpoints.note: Rice in China, potatoes in the Andes and maize in Mexico are bred from wild plants, and cats and chickens settle near farms.

checkpoints.name: Beasts of burden
checkpoints.note: Llamas, horses and camels carry loads and people, silkworms give silk, tea is grown in China, and bananas spread across the tropics.

checkpoints.name: Global crops
checkpoints.note: Coffee, sugar and cotton spread across the world through trade and empire, the Columbian exchange moves crops between the hemispheres, and growing one variety everywhere makes crops easy prey for disease.
